claims.claim: The paper evaluates a Behavioral Specification alongside full raw corpus, full extracted facts, and four commercial memory systems: Mem0, Letta, Supermemory, and Zep.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Across 14 public-domain autobiographical corpora, the Specification lifted representational accuracy in aggregate and nearly eliminated model hedging.
claims.quote: Across 14 public-domain autobiographical corpora, the Specification lifts representational accuracy in aggregate and nearly eliminates model hedging.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The Specification recovers most of what the raw corpus delivers at about 25 times less context cost.
claims.quote: It recovers most of what the raw corpus delivers, at ~25x less context cost.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The lift is greatest on interpretation-required questions, where an interpretive layer enables model behavior that extracted facts or raw corpus do not.
claims.quote: Lift is greatest on interpretation-required questions, where providing an interpretive layer enables model behavior that extracted facts or raw corpus do not.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: On recall-required questions, the interpretive layer can interfere rather than help.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: The paper concludes that representational accuracy is distinct from recall and that human-AI alignment depends on how accurately the user is represented.
claims.quote: We conclude that representational accuracy is distinct from recall and that human-AI alignment is dependent on how accurately the user is represented.
